Legendary creatures printed as backup commanders in preconstructed decks, with the same color identity as the face commander.

Ante is a depreciated game mechanic where players would remove the top card of their deck from the game and give it to their opponent if they lose. Some early cards in magic would have effects that allowed players to ante more cards for effects.
Your entire team gets +N/+N. Possibly limited to creature types or colors.
Abilities that can be activated by anyone.
Cards that change the colour of things in any and every zone.
These cards change types in every and any zone.
Deals X damage divided as you choose among one, two, or three targets.
You and an opponent pick a creature you own, then they fight! (Or kiss, in the tunnel of love)

An ability in which the P/T of one or more creatures can increase based on the number of equipment attached to one creature outside of the equipment's effects of being attached. See also [cranial plating](cranial-plating).
A toughness-pumping ability. See also [firebreathing] in red and [shade pump] in black.
Cards which care about the contents of art. See also [artist matters](/tags/card/artist-matters).

Effects that turn things into artifacts.

Effects that attempt to equalize the board state between players by forcing players to sacrifice permanents on the battlefield or discard their cards to a number set by the player with the fewest on the field or in hand.

A creature gets a power boost, but will die this turn.

Effects which are iconically black.
Block additional creatures beyond just the one.
Effects that trigger on a creature blocking or becoming blocked.
Block an unlimited, or practically unlimited, number of creatures.
These cards make something be blocked ... without anything actually doing the blocking.

Derived from the titular card, this refers to the effect in which lands lose their land type and/or abilities, being replaced by something else.
Effects which are iconically blue.
Cards that remove the entire battlefield.
Lands you can pay 3 life/take 3 damage to have them enter untapped.
Sacrifice something else to deal N damage. See also [fling](/tags/card/fling), [bombard-self](bombard-self).
Sacrifice this permanent to deal N damage. See also [fling-self](/tags/card/fling-self), [bombard](bombard).
Cards, usually acorn cards, that have you open booster packs to add into the game.
Cards that give themselves or other creatures keyword abilities if something else has it. See also [keyword soup](keyword-soup).

Repeatable effects that, if an arbitrary amount of mana is dumped into them, will probably win you the game—for example, by drawing your whole deck, creating an arbitrarily large attacker, making an endless army of tokens, gaining infinite life, etc.

Auras you can bounce back to your hand.
Non-basic lands which tap for two mana, but require you to return a land to your hand when you play them.
Draw a number of cards, then put cards from your hand on top of your library in any order.

Cards with morph (or a similar ability) which break the Khans of Tarkir block development rule which stated that a morphed creature cannot be turned face-up for less than five mana if doing so would allow it to win combat against a face-down morphed creature.
Give an opponent something in exchange for a benefit to you.
A vehicle (or spacecraft) that comes with a built-in pilot to crew (or station) it.
Mana that comes with additional benefits when spent.

Effects that deal damage, whether to creatures, players, or planeswalkers.
Cards that burn any target: players, creatures, battles, or planeswalkers.
Cards like [Burn Bright](https://scryfall.com/card/rna/93/burn-bright) or [Trumpet Blast](https://scryfall.com/card/m10/160/trumpet-blast), but with the set's mechanic.
Creatures deal damage to themselves.
Burn spells that have the mechanic of the set they debuted in.
Sometimes your own cards hurt you the most.

Card draw effects that can net you a bunch of cards at once. As a rule of thumb, to qualify for this tag, the card should let you draw at least three cards at a time and come out ahead by at least +1.
